The indirect effect is significant: the interval does not contain zero. The interval is a percentile bootstrap from 5,000 resamples with a fixed seed, so the same data always give the same interval. The total effect c equals the direct effect c′ plus the indirect effect a × b. The standardised value is a × b multiplied by the SD of X and divided by the SD of Y. Mediation is a claim about causes. The statistics show whether the pattern fits the chain X → M → Y. The p-values of the a, b and c paths are ordinary regression tests; the indirect effect is judged by its bootstrap interval.

A mediation analysis with a percentile bootstrap (5,000 resamples) showed that the indirect effect of stress on grades through sleep was significant, ab = 0.304, 95% CI [0.143, 0.473]. stress significantly predicted sleep (a = 0.35, p < .001), and sleep significantly predicted grades when stress was controlled (b = 0.87, p < .001). The direct effect was c′ = 0.07 (p = .493) and the total effect was c = 0.38 (p < .001).

The direct effect was c′ = 2.92 (p = .582) and the total effect was c = 0.91 (p = .859).
